children: Russia's consumer inflation increased to 0.96% in the week to October 5 from 0.12% in the previous week, driven by a planned increase in regulated utility tariffs, data released on Wednesday showed.

Russia annually raises tariffs for electricity, gas, heating and water, but this year the increase was moved from July to October following a parliamentary election. Utility tariffs are expected to rise by 9.9% on average this year, compared with an 11.9% increase last year.
The tariff hike pushed cumulative inflation since the start of the year up to 5.94%, compared with the 6.00-7.00% target.
Last month, the central bank halted its cycle of key rate cuts, warning of rising inflationary risks and an acceleration in underlying price growth.
